subject: JAGS error in N-mixture Neg Binomial with detection overdispersion

messages.author: b3061e9ec8f1a7f2
messages.subject: JAGS error in N-mixture Neg Binomial with detection overdispersion
parts:
Hi all,

I'm experimenting with various N-mixture models and have come across an error I can't figure out.  I am sampling a critter at 38 locations with up to 3 surveys per location.  Three locations only have one observation.  I'm using a negative binomial for abundance and modeling detection as overdispersed.  When using the full data set, JAGS throws an error, "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'jags::NodeError' what():  Failure to calculate log density"

If I remove the locations with only one observation, this error goes away. 

With the full data set, if I model abundance with poisson, and detection with overdispersion, no error.  If I model abundance with neg binomial and detection without overdispereion,  no error.

I've attached some code.

Thoughts?
Brian

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: JAGS error in N-mixture Neg Binomial with detection overdispersion
parts:
Dear Brian,

I have had that error from time to time. I think it means that internally JAGS encountered a division by zero or something similar. You could experiment with different parameterizations or perhaps slightly more concentrated priors and hope it goes away also for the model of your choice.

Best regards  --- Marc
